+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Minimal compiler for a tiny expression language (.k files).
+
+Grammar:
+    program := "return" expr ";"
+    expr    := term (("+" | "-") term)*
+    term    := unary (("*" | "/") unary)*
+    unary   := "-" unary | primary
+    primary := INTEGER | "(" expr ")"
+
+Emits x86-64 (AT&T syntax) assembly defining main(); the expression's value
+becomes the process exit status, truncated to 0-255 by the OS.
+
+Usage: python3 src/compiler.py INPUT.k -o OUTPUT.s
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+
+
+def tokenize(source):
+    """Split source into (kind, value) tokens; kinds: int, kw, punct, eof."""
+    tokens = []
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(source):
+        ch = source[i]
+        if ch.isspace():
+            i += 1
+        elif ch.isdigit():
+            j = i
+            while j < len(source) and source[j].isdigit():
+                j += 1
+            tokens.append(("int", source[i:j]))
+            i = j
+        elif ch.isalpha():
+            j = i
+            while j < len(source) and source[j].isalnum():
+                j += 1
+            tokens.append(("kw", source[i:j]))
+            i = j
+        elif ch in "+-*/();":
+            tokens.append(("punct", ch))
+            i += 1
+        else:
+            raise SyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at offset {i}")
+    tokens.append(("eof", ""))
+    return tokens
+
+
+class Parser:
+    """Recursive-descent parser producing nested-tuple ASTs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tokens):
+        self.tokens = tokens
+        self.pos = 0
+
+    def peek(self):
+        return self.tokens[self.pos]
+
+    def advance(self):
+        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
+        self.pos += 1
+        return tok
+
+    def expect(self, kind, value):
+        tok = self.advance()
+        if tok != (kind, value):
+            wanted = "end of input" if kind == "eof" else repr(value)
+            raise SyntaxError(f"expected {wanted}, got {tok[1]!r}")
+        return tok
+
+    def parse_program(self):
+        self.expect("kw", "return")
+        expr = self.parse_expr()
+        self.expect("punct", ";")
+        self.expect("eof", "")
+        return ("return", expr)
+
+    def parse_expr(self):
+        node = self.parse_term()
+        while self.peek() in (("punct", "+"), ("punct", "-")):
+            op = self.advance()[1]
+            node = (op, node, self.parse_term())
+        return node
+
+    def parse_term(self):
+        node = self.parse_unary()
+        while self.peek() in (("punct", "*"), ("punct", "/")):
+            op = self.advance()[1]
+            node = (op, node, self.parse_unary())
+        return node
+
+    def parse_unary(self):
+        if self.peek() == ("punct", "-"):
+            self.advance()
+            return ("neg", self.parse_unary())
+        return self.parse_primary()
+
+    def parse_primary(self):
+        tok = self.advance()
+        if tok[0] == "int":
+            return ("int", int(tok[1]))
+        if tok == ("punct", "("):
+            node = self.parse_expr()
+            self.expect("punct", ")")
+            return node
+        if tok[0] == "eof":
+            raise SyntaxError("unexpected end of input")
+        raise SyntaxError(f"unexpected token {tok[1]!r}")
+
+
+INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX = -(2**31), 2**31 - 1
+
+
+def generate(node, lines):
+    """Emit code that evaluates `node` into %rax."""
+    kind = node[0]
+    if kind == "int":
+        value = node[1]
+        if not INT32_MIN <= value <= INT32_MAX:
+            raise SyntaxError(f"integer literal {value} does not fit in 32 bits")
+        lines.append(f"    movq ${value}, %rax")
+    elif kind == "neg":
+        generate(node[1], lines)
+        lines.append("    negq %rax")
+    elif kind in "+-*/":
+        generate(node[1], lines)        # left  -> %rax
+        lines.append("    pushq %rax")
+        generate(node[2], lines)        # right -> %rax
+        lines.append("    popq %rcx")   # %rcx = left, %rax = right
+        if kind == "+":
+            lines.append("    addq %rcx, %rax")
+        elif kind == "-":
+            lines.append("    subq %rax, %rcx")
+            lines.append("    movq %rcx, %rax")
+        elif kind == "*":
+            lines.append("    imulq %rcx, %rax")
+        else:  # "/"
+            lines.append("    xchgq %rax, %rcx")
+            lines.append("    cqto")          # sign-extend %rax into %rdx:%rax
+            lines.append("    idivq %rcx")    # quotient -> %rax
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError(f"unknown AST node {kind!r}")
+
+
+def compile_source(source):
+    ast = Parser(tokenize(source)).parse_program()
+    lines = ["    .text", "    .globl main", "main:"]
+    generate(ast[1], lines)
+    lines.append("    ret")
+    lines.append('')
+    lines.append('    .section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits')
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Compile a .k program to x86-64 assembly."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("input", help="source file (.k)")
+    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True, help="output assembly file")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+
+    with open(args.input) as f:
+        source = f.read()
+
+    try:
+        asm = compile_source(source)
+    except SyntaxError as exc:
+        print(f"{args.input}: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    with open(args.output, "w") as f:
+        f.write(asm)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Test the compiler: compile each example, assemble/link it, run it, and
+# compare the exit status (the program's value, mod 256) with the expectation.
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+
+BUILD=build
+COMPILER=src/compiler.py
+pass=0
+fail=0
+mkdir -p "$BUILD"
+
+check() {
+    local name="$1" expected="$2"
+    local asm="$BUILD/$name.s" exe="$BUILD/$name"
+
+    if ! python3 "$COMPILER" "examples/$name.k" -o "$asm"; then
+        echo "FAIL $name: compiler error"
+        fail=$((fail + 1))
+        return
+    fi
+    if ! gcc -Wall -o "$exe" "$asm"; then
+        echo "FAIL $name: assembly/link error"
+        fail=$((fail + 1))
+        return
+    fi
+
+    local status=0
+    "$exe" || status=$?
+    if [ "$status" -eq "$expected" ]; then
+        echo "PASS $name (exit $status)"
+        pass=$((pass + 1))
+    else
+        echo "FAIL $name: expected exit $expected, got $status"
+        fail=$((fail + 1))
+    fi
+}
+
+check return42 42    # return 42;
+check arith 14       # return 2 + 3 * 4;      (precedence)
+check parens 9       # return (1 + 2) * 3;    (grouping)
+check sub 5          # return 10 - 3 - 2;     (left-associative)
+check division 12    # return 84 / 7;         (integer division)
+check unary 252      # return -4;             (exit statuses are mod 256)
+
+# Negative test: invalid source must be rejected with a nonzero exit.
+if python3 "$COMPILER" examples/bad.k -o "$BUILD/bad.s" 2>"$BUILD/bad.err"; then
+    echo "FAIL bad.k: compiler accepted invalid input"
+    fail=$((fail + 1))
+else
+    echo "PASS bad.k (rejected: $(cat "$BUILD/bad.err"))"
+    pass=$((pass + 1))
+fi
+
+echo
+echo "$pass passed, $fail failed"
+[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
